architecture.text:
PART 1 — ARCHITECTURE SUMMARY

PRODUCT IDENTITY
- Headline: "404 | Page Not Found"
- One-line pitch (from meta description): "An AI-powered tool to help you understand and reduce your environmental impact."

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
- The page has no functional primary objective in its current state. It is a 404 error page, and its sole recoverable action is to redirect the visitor back to the homepage via a "Go Home" link. No conversion, sign-up, or informational goal is being served.

INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE
- 1. Page title bar / browser tab: "app | SAIGE"
- 2. Primary error heading (h1): "404"
- 3. Secondary error descriptor (h2): "Page Not Found"
- 4. Explanatory body text: 'The page "app" could not be found in this application.'
- 5. Recovery navigation: "Go Home" link

CONTENT INVENTORY
- Visible CTAs: "Go Home"
- Visible forms or input affordances: None detected. No search field, no email capture, no login form present on this error page.
- Trust signals: None. No logos, testimonials, partner badges, user statistics, or social proof elements are present on this error page.

TECH SIGNALS
- JavaScript rendering required (captured via browserless/JS-rendered method), suggesting a client-side or hybrid framework such as Next.js, Nuxt, or a similar SPA/SSR framework.
- The URL path structure (/app) and the error message phrasing ("could not be found in this application") are consistent with Next.js or similar React-based routing conventions.
- No CDN, hosting provider, or performance-specific signals are discernible from the truncated body content alone.
- Meta description is present and populated, suggesting at least basic SEO configuration is in place at the framework level.

ACCESSIBILITY SIGNALS
- Heading hierarchy is irregular for an error page: h1 contains "404" (a numeric code rather than a descriptive label) and h2 contains "Page Not Found" (more descriptive). Reversing or combining these would better serve screen reader users.
- No alt-text presence can be confirmed or denied from the available content; no images are referenced in the captured body.
- Contrast indicators cannot be assessed from text content alone; no inline styles or class names indicating color choices are present in the truncated capture.
- The single navigation element ("Go Home") appears to be a plain text link, which should be keyboard-accessible if properly implemented.

QUALITY SCORE: 4/100
- This page scores extremely low because it is a broken 404 error state delivering zero intended content, no conversion pathways, no trust signals, and no substantive information architecture beyond a minimal error message and a single recovery link, making it essentially non-functional as a product or landing page.

improvement_plan.text:
PART 1 — IMPROVEMENT PLAN (plain text, no markdown bold):

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The single biggest opportunity is to transform this dead-end 404 error page into a lightweight recovery and acquisition surface by surfacing the product's core value proposition, a working app entry point, and at minimum one conversion pathway, converting an otherwise total loss visit into a potential user. The single biggest risk is that the /app route being broken suggests a routing or deployment misconfiguration that may be actively blocking users who were sent a direct link to the product, meaning every marketing, referral, or onboarding email pointing to /app is silently failing and losing real users right now.

PRIORITIZED IMPROVEMENTS (max 7)

[P0] [technical] fix-broken-app-route — The /app route is returning a 404 despite being the canonical product URL referenced in the page title, indicating a deployment, routing, or authentication misconfiguration that must be resolved immediately; audit the Next.js or SPA router configuration to ensure /app either renders the authenticated app shell, redirects to a login page, or correctly serves the intended entry point.

[P0] [conversion] add-working-app-entry-cta — The 404 page offers zero path to the actual product; replace or supplement the "Go Home" link with a direct "Try SAIGE" or "Get Started" CTA that routes to the correct, functioning app or sign-up flow.

[P1] [technical] audit-inbound-link-integrity — Any marketing materials, email campaigns, social links, or SEO-indexed pages pointing to /app are currently sending users to a dead end; run a full inbound link audit and either fix the destination URL or implement a 301 redirect from /app to the correct authenticated entry point.

[P1] [copy] rewrite-404-page-messaging — The current error copy is generic and cold; rewrite it to reflect the SAIGE brand voice, acknowledge the user's intent ("Looks like you were trying to reach the SAIGE app"), and immediately re-orient them with a clear next step that reinforces the product's environmental impact value proposition.

[P1] [design] elevate-404-page-to-branded-recovery-surface — The page has no visual identity, trust signals, or brand presence; add the SAIGE logo, a brief one-line product description, and at least two navigation options such as login, sign up, and learn more so the page functions as a minimal but credible brand touchpoint rather than a dead end.

[P2] [trust] surface-social-proof-or-value-signal — Even on a 404 page, a single data point or short testimonial such as "Join X users already reducing their carbon footprint" would maintain credibility and reduce bounce intent; add one quantified trust signal pulled from existing marketing assets.

[P2] [compliance] fix-heading-hierarchy-for-accessibility — The current h1 contains only the numeric code "404" which is non-descriptive for screen readers; change h1 to "Page Not Found" and demote the numeric code to a visually prominent span or aria-hidden decorative element to comply with WCAG 2.1 heading structure guidance.

QUICK WINS (max 3)

1. Update the h1 from "404" to "Page Not Found" and move the numeric code to a styled decorative element, resolving the heading hierarchy accessibility issue in under 15 minutes with a single template file edit.

2. Add a second CTA button alongside "Go Home" that reads "Go to the App" pointing to the correct working route or login URL, requiring only a one-line link addition to the 404 template.

3. Add the SAIGE logo and the meta description tagline as visible body text on the 404 page to restore brand context for confused visitors, achievable by editing the error page component in under 30 minutes.

STRUCTURAL CHANGES (max 3)

1. Investigate and resolve the root cause of the /app route returning 404, which likely requires an engineering review of the deployment pipeline, authentication middleware, and router configuration to determine whether the route was never deployed, is gated behind auth without a redirect, or was accidentally deleted in a recent release.

2. Design and implement a fully branded 404 page component that includes the logo, a short empathetic headline, a product value statement, at least two recovery navigation options, and optionally a search field or sitemap shortcut, requiring a design pass and a front-end component build estimated at two to four hours.

3. Implement a server-side or client-side redirect rule mapping /app to the correct authenticated entry point or onboarding flow, and set up automated broken-link monitoring using a tool such as Sentry, Ahrefs alerts, or a synthetic uptime check so future route regressions are caught before users encounter them.

QUALITY SCORE: 61/100
The plan is constrained by extremely thin input data; the captured page is a pure error state with no product UI, no user flows, and no real content to analyze, so all recommendations are necessarily inferential. The score reflects high confidence in the P0 technical findings and recovery UX recommendations, discounted significantly because no actual product architecture, conversion funnel, or design system information was available to ground deeper strategic guidance.
